label: lem:continuous_integrable
title: Continuous functions are interval integrable
statement: If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous on the interval $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, then $f$ is interval integrable on $[a, b]$ with respect to the Lebesgue measure. In Mathlib this follows from \texttt{ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable}.
proof: Direct application of \texttt{ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable}: a continuous function on a compact interval is bounded and measurable, hence integrable with respect to the Lebesgue measure.
